entities.name: Boc-N-methyl-GABA
observations: SELFIES decoding gives CN(CCCC(=O)O)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, a Boc-protected N-methyl-4-aminobutyric acid.
The carboxylic acid is the group transformed into an amide in the product.

entities.name: Nitrophenylenediamine
observations: SELFIES decoding gives NC1=CC=CC([N+](=O)[O-])=C1N, a nitro-phenylenediamine with two aryl amino groups.
One aryl amino group is acylated while the other remains as NH2 in the product.

entities.name: ORD-9961e7a62ca84c3a8fba3cbea619a658
observations: Exact ORD product match supports coupling Boc-protected N-methyl-4-aminobutyric acid with nitro-phenylenediamine to form the observed aryl amide.
The indexed record lists DIPEA, HOBt, sodium bicarbonate, dichloromethane, and 1,2-dichloroethane; a conventional carbodiimide or uronium reagent is not explicitly indexed.

entities.name: Amide coupling conditions
observations: Plausible conditions are acid 1.0 equivalent, nitro-phenylenediamine 1.0–1.2 equivalents, DIPEA 2–4 equivalents, HOBt or Oxyma 1.1–1.5 equivalents, and DMF or chlorinated solvent, adding at 0 °C then warming to room temperature.
Alternative coupling systems include EDCI·HCl/HOBt or Oxyma/DIPEA, HATU/DIPEA, HBTU/DIPEA, and T3P/DIPEA.
Because the diamine has two aryl amino groups, controlled stoichiometry and short reaction time reduce bis-acylation; selective protection may be needed for regioselectivity.
